verdict.rationale: Loops documents event-triggered workflows. Users or agents send events through the API to start published workflows, and workflow graphs (nodes, branches, mailing-list changes) can be created and edited from code or triggered by incoming webhooks. The evidence is first-party marketing and API docs only, and the branching rule logic is described only briefly. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, detailed documentation of trigger conditions and branch rules, and actions beyond email and mailing-list changes.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: POST /events/send Send an event to trigger workflows
Create and update workflow graphs, change mailing lists, and add, branch, edit, or delete nodes from code. Send events to start published workflows.
Build onboarding, trial, and re-engagement workflows around your product events.
